items.title: Armand Hug Interview, 1960-07-14
items.q: I'm trying to think of a fellow there that played piano with Abbot Murness at that time.

ctx.x: And Sidney never gets any credit for it. He never gets any credit for it. But he sure did play a nice tone. He had a good, beautiful, beautiful tone and wonderful ideas. Well you know he had wonderful ideas to write a tune like Blazy River.

That's just an idea right there of some of the ideas that he had. I followed a piano player in there you're talking about. I know you've known since I'm on the subject of piano players. I know you want to bring out some of the old names that Warren brought out. I'm trying to think of a fellow there that played piano with Abbot Murness at that time. He was a real fine guy. One of these real comical sort of guys. Always wanting to improve his playing. Never did get to be real great but he was a real ambitious sort…
See, he sang on some too, Red Long. I don't know if Red sang on them.
